source_text:
Καὶ ὑμῖν δὲ πρέπει μὴ συγχρᾶσθαι τῇ ἡλικίᾳ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου, ἀλλὰ κατὰ δύναμιν θεοῦ πατρὸς πᾶσαν ἐντροπὴν αὐτῷ ἀπονέμειν, καθὼς ἔγνων καὶ τοὺς ἁγίους πρεσβυτέρους οὐ προσειληφότας τὴν φαινομένην νεωτερικὴν τάξιν, ἀλλ’ ὡς φρονίμους ἐν θεῷ συγχωροῦντας αὐτῷ, οὐκ αὐτῷ δέ, ἀλλὰ τῷ πατρὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τῷ πάντων ἐπισκόπῳ.
εἰς τιμὴν οὖν ἐκείνου τοῦ θελήσαντος ἡμᾶς πρέπον ἐστὶν ἐπακούειν κατὰ μηδεμίαν ὑπόκρισιν: ἐπεὶ οὐχ ὅτι τὸν ἐπίσκοπον τοῦτον τὸν βλεπόμενον πλανᾷ τις, ἀλλὰ τὸν ἀόρατον παραλογίζεται. τὸ δὲ τοιοῦτον οὐ πρὸς σάρκα ὁ λόγος, ἀλλὰ πρὸς θεὸν τὸν τὰ κρύφια εἰδότα.
thought_title: Honor the bishop as God's hidden overseer
orientation: Ignatius is addressing the Magnesians, urging them to honor their bishop Damas not by his apparent youth but as one who stands in for God the Father.
pass_a_gloss: And for you also it is fitting not to be misled by the age of the bishop, but according to the power of God the Father to give every respect to him, just as I have known also the holy council of elders not taking advantage of the apparent youthful rank, but as wise men in God yielding to him, not to him however, but to the Father of Jesus Christ, the bishop of all. For the honor therefore of him who willed us, it is fitting to obey with no hypocrisy: since not that this bishop who is seen someone deceives, but the invisible one he cheats. And such a thing is not toward flesh the word, but toward God who knows the hidden things.

choices.english: to take advantage of the age
choices.why: The verb means to use something for one's own benefit; here it means exploiting the bishop's youth as an excuse not to honor him.
rejected: to be presumptuous about the age

choices.why: ἐντροπή is honor or deference; ἀπονέμειν means to assign or render what is due.
φαινομένην means what appears to the eye; νεωτερικὴν τάξιν is the youthful position or status of the bishop.
The participle describes the elders deferring to the bishop rather than asserting themselves over him.
ἐπίσκοπος is the glossary term for bishop; here it is applied to God the Father as the one who oversees all.
The verb means to defraud or deceive by false reasoning; it intensifies the deception against the invisible God.

pass_b_english: It is fitting for you too not to take advantage of the bishop's age, but to give him all respect according to the power of God the Father. I have learned that the holy council of elders did not despise his apparent youthful rank, but as wise men in God yielded to him. Yet they yielded not to him, but to the Father of Jesus Christ, who is bishop of all.

So for the honor of the one who willed us, it is fitting to obey with no hypocrisy at all. For such a person does not merely deceive this bishop who is seen, but cheats the One who is unseen. And in such a matter the word is not about flesh, but about God, who knows the hidden things.

problems.quote: not to take advantage of the bishop's age
problems.source_quote: μὴ συγχρᾶσθαι τῇ ἡλικίᾳ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου
problems.why: Greek means ‘not to be confused or misled by the bishop’s age’, not ‘take advantage of’
problems.fix: not to be misled by the bishop’s age

edits.old: not to take advantage of the bishop's age
edits.new: not to be misled by the bishop's age

fixed: Changed 'take advantage of' to 'be misled by' in both the English and the literal gloss, matching the Greek συγχρᾶσθαι in this context.

problems.quote: not to be misled by the bishop's age
problems.source_quote: μὴ συγχρᾶσθαι τῇ ἡλικίᾳ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου
problems.why: συγχρᾶσθαι means 'to deal with/use/associate with,' not 'be misled by.' The sense is 'not to judge by his age.'
problems.fix: not to judge by the bishop's age
problems.ruling: Greek says ‘not to be swayed/associated with the bishop’s age’, not a deception‑implied ‘misled by’

problems.quote: did not take advantage of his apparent youthful rank
problems.source_quote: οὐ προσειληφότας τὴν φαινομένην νεωτερικὴν τάξιν
problems.why: προσέρχομαι/προσλαμβάνω here means 'to take up/accept,' not 'take advantage of.' They did not accept his apparent youthful rank.
problems.fix: did not accept his apparent youthful rank
problems.ruling: Greek participle means ‘did not accept/take up the apparent youthful rank’, not ‘take advantage of’

edits.old: not to be misled by the bishop's age
edits.new: not to judge by the bishop's age

edits.old: did not take advantage of his apparent youthful rank
edits.new: did not accept his apparent youthful rank

problems.why: Same office rendered three ways; readers may think 'elders' and 'presbyters' differ from 'council of elders.'
problems.fix: Use one term consistently, e.g., 'council of elders' throughout.

edits.old: the holy elders did not accept his apparent youthful rank
edits.new: the holy council of elders did not accept his apparent youthful rank

fixed: Changed 'elders' to 'council of elders' to use one consistent term for the office.

problems.quote: For it is not that someone deceives this bishop who is seen, but he cheats the one who is invisible
problems.why: Double negative and pronoun confusion; 'not that someone deceives' obscures meaning.
problems.fix: Revise: 'For it is not the visible bishop who is deceived, but the invisible One [God] whom they cheat.'

edits.old: For it is not that someone deceives this bishop who is seen, but he cheats the one who is invisible.
edits.new: For it is not the visible bishop who is deceived, but the invisible One whom they cheat.

fixed: The earlier attempted edits to 'not to take advantage of the bishop's age' and 'did not take advantage of his apparent youthful rank' were not confirmed problems in the current English; the only confirmed problem was the double negative and pronoun confusion in the sentence about deceiving the bishop, which has been revised.

problems.quote: For it is not the visible bishop who is deceived, but the invisible One whom they cheat.
problems.why: Logic inverted: should be 'it is not the visible bishop who is deceived' but 'the invisible One whom they cheat' doesn't parallel; seems to mean 'they do not deceive the visible bishop but cheat the invisible God'.
problems.fix: Revise: 'For it is not the visible bishop they deceive, but the invisible One whom they cheat.'

edits.old: For it is not the visible bishop who is deceived, but the invisible One whom they cheat.
edits.new: For it is not the visible bishop they deceive, but the invisible One whom they cheat.

problems.why: 'Council of elders' vs plain 'elders' may seem different institutions; 'council of the apostles' is analogical.
problems.fix: Consistently use 'council of elders' or note equivalence.

problems.quote: For such a person does not deceive this bishop who is seen, but cheats the One who is unseen.
problems.why: Logic inverted: 'such a person' = hypocrite; sentence says they don't deceive visible bishop but cheat unseen God—should be 'does not deceive [merely] the visible bishop.'
problems.fix: 'does not merely deceive the visible bishop, but cheats God who is unseen.'

edits.old: For such a person does not deceive this bishop who is seen, but cheats the One who is unseen.
edits.new: For such a person does not merely deceive this bishop who is seen, but cheats the One who is unseen.

fixed: The glossary issue is not a translation error; 'council of elders' is the required rendering for πρεσβυτέριον, and the English already uses it consistently.

The source (ἐπεὶ οὐχ ὅτι τὸν ἐπίσκοπον τοῦτον τὸν βλεπόμενον πλανᾷ τις, ἀλλὰ τὸν ἀόρατον παραλογίζεται) means the hypocrite does not merely deceive the visible bishop but cheats the unseen God; added 'merely' to correct the logic.

last_rejected.quote: did not accept his apparent youthful rank
last_rejected.source_quote: οὐ προσειληφότας τὴν φαινομένην νεωτερικὴν τάξιν
last_rejected.why: Source says elders did not accept/receive the apparent youthful order; English says they did not accept the bishop's rank.
last_rejected.fix: did not accept the apparent youthful order
last_rejected.ruling: Greek says elders did not receive the apparent youthful order; English says they did not accept his apparent youthful rank—equivalent meaning.

last_rejected.quote: For it is not that someone deceives this bishop who is seen, but he cheats the one who is invisible.
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐπεὶ οὐχ ὅτι τὸν ἐπίσκοπον τοῦτον τὸν βλεπόμενον πλανᾷ τις, ἀλλὰ τὸν ἀόρατον παραλογίζεται.
last_rejected.why: Source: one who deceives the visible bishop cheats the invisible God. English 'he cheats' could refer to the bishop, not the deceiver.
last_rejected.fix: but he cheats the one who is invisible, the deceiver himself.
last_rejected.ruling: Greek: not that anyone deceives the visible bishop but deceives the invisible; English conveys same sense, despite pronoun ambiguity.

last_rejected.quote: as wise men in God yielded to him
last_rejected.source_quote: ὡς φρονίμους ἐν θεῷ συγχωροῦντας αὐτῷ
last_rejected.why: Greek says they are in fellowship/association with him, not that they yield to him.
last_rejected.fix: as wise men in God who associate with him
last_rejected.ruling: συγχωροῦντας can mean 'yield/permit/agree'; rendering as 'yielded' is within normal range, not a clear mistranslation.

polish.changed: Clarified that the elders yielded to the Father, not to the bishop, and identified the Father as 'who is bishop of all' to avoid confusion with a human bishop. Broke the long first sentence into shorter ones and made the implied subject of 'yielded' explicit.

notes.why: This phrase for God the Father is ambiguous and could be mistaken for a human bishop.
notes.fix: Clarify that 'the bishop of all' refers to God the Father, not a human office-holder.

polish.changed: Clarified the logic of the deception sentence by making the parallel direct: they do not deceive the visible bishop but cheat the invisible God. Also smoothed sentence flow and kept all claims, qualifications, and references intact.

notes.quote: For it is not the visible bishop who is deceived, but the invisible One whom they cheat.
notes.why: Logic inverted: should be 'it is not the visible bishop who is deceived' but 'the invisible One whom they cheat' doesn't parallel; seems to mean 'they do not deceive the visible bishop but cheat the invisible God'.
notes.fix: Revise: 'For it is not the visible bishop they deceive, but the invisible One whom they cheat.'

polish.changed: Clarified that the council of elders did not despise the bishop's youthful rank, made the subject of the deception explicit, and smoothed the sentence flow for modern readers.

notes.quote: the holy council of elders did not seize on his apparent youthful rank
notes.why: 'Seize on' is wrong idiom; means 'take advantage of' but context requires 'were not put off by' or 'did not despise'.
notes.fix: Revise to 'did not despise his apparent youth' or 'did not take advantage of his youth'.
